Every example below is shown twice. The left column is what you type. The right
column is what the reader sees.

## Headings

A heading is a line that starts with one to six `#` characters, followed by a
space. One `#` is the title of the document, `##` is a section, `###` a
subsection, and so on. Leave a blank line before and after a heading.

::: {.grid .md-demo}
::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
````markdown
# Title

## Section 1

### Subsection

## Section 2

### Subsection


````
:::
::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
<h1>Title</h1>
<h2>Section 1</h2>
<h3>Subsection</h3>
<h2>Section 2</h2>
<h3>Subsection</h3>
:::
:::

Don't skip levels: a `###` belongs under a `##`, not directly under a `#`. Most
documents need only two or three levels.

## Paragraphs

A paragraph is one or more lines of text. Paragraphs are separated by a blank
line --- that blank line is the only thing that matters. A single line break
inside a paragraph is ignored, so you are free to wrap your source text at
whatever width you find comfortable.

::: {.grid .md-demo}
::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
````markdown
Programs must be written for people to
read, and only incidentally for
machines to execute.

That sentence is from the preface of
SICP.
````
:::
::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
Programs must be written for people to
read, and only incidentally for
machines to execute.

That sentence is from the preface of
SICP.
:::
:::

If you really need a line break within a paragraph, end the line with a
backslash.

::: {.grid .md-demo}
::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
````markdown
Roses are red \
Violets are blue
````
:::
::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
Roses are red \
Violets are blue
:::
:::

## Formatting

Wrap text in one asterisk for *emphasis*, two for **strong emphasis**, and
backticks for `code` --- names of commands, files, variables and anything else
that should be read literally.

::: {.grid .md-demo}
::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
````markdown
This is *italic*, this is **bold**, and
this is ***both***.

Run `ls -l` to list files in the
current directory.

You can also ~~strike out~~ text.
````
:::
::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
This is *italic*, this is **bold**, and
this is ***both***.

Run `ls -l` to list files in the
current directory.

You can also ~~strike out~~ text.
:::
:::

Use `>` at the start of a line to quote someone.

::: {.grid .md-demo}
::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
````markdown
> Simplicity is prerequisite for
> reliability.
>
> --- Edsger Dijkstra
````
:::
::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
> Simplicity is prerequisite for
> reliability.
>
> --- Edsger Dijkstra
:::
:::

## Lists

An unordered list is a set of lines starting with `-`. An ordered list starts
with `1.`, `2.` and so on. Indent by four spaces to nest one list inside
another.

::: {.grid .md-demo}
::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
````markdown
- the shell
- a text editor
- version control
    - git
    - a place to push it
````
:::
::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
- the shell
- a text editor
- version control
    - git
    - a place to push it
:::
:::

::: {.grid .md-demo}
::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
````markdown
1. Read the problem
2. Write the smallest thing that runs
3. Make it correct
4. Make it clear
````
:::
::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
1. Read the problem
2. Write the smallest thing that runs
3. Make it correct
4. Make it clear
:::
:::

The numbers you type are not the numbers you get --- the output is numbered in
sequence regardless. Writing `1.` on every line is a common habit, because then
inserting an item in the middle costs nothing.

## Links

A link is the text in square brackets followed by the address in parentheses.
A bare URL in angle brackets becomes a link to itself.

::: {.grid .md-demo}
::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
````markdown
[DuckDuckGo](https://duckduckgo.com/) is my favorite seach engine.

I use it insead of [Google](https://google.com/).
````
:::
::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
[DuckDuckGo](https://duckduckgo.com/) is my favorite seach engine.

I use it insead of [Google](https://google.com/).
:::
:::

The links to be used to link other relative resources.

::: {.grid .md-demo}
::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
````markdown
[Download the slides](slides.pdf).
````
:::
::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
[Download the slides](slides.pdf).
:::
:::

We could use the links to create a simple navigation.

::: {.grid .md-demo}
::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
````markdown
# My Blog
[About](about.html) | [Contact](contact.html)
````
:::
::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
<h1>My Blog</h1>

[About](about.html) | [Contact](contact.html)
:::
:::



## Images

An image is a link with a `!` in front of it. The text in the square brackets is
the alt text --- a description read aloud by screen readers and shown when the
image fails to load. Write it as a sentence describing what the image shows.

::: {.grid .md-demo}
::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
````markdown
A Sample local image:

![](images/sample.svg)

An xkcd cartoon from the web:

![](https://imgs.xkcd.com/comics/final_exam.png)

````
:::
::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
A Sample local image:

![](images/sample.svg)

An xkcd cartoon from the web:

![](https://imgs.xkcd.com/comics/final_exam.png)
:::
:::

## Code Blocks

Wrap code in a line of three backticks above and below it.

::: {.grid .md-demo}
::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
`````
```
$ seq 5
1
2
3
4
5
```
`````
:::
::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
```
$ seq 5
1
2
3
4
5
```
:::
:::

## Math Expressions

Mathematics is written in LaTeX notation. Put it between single dollar signs to
keep it in the flow of a sentence, or between double dollar signs to set it on
its own line.

::: {.grid .md-demo}
::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
````markdown
The area of a circle is $\pi r^2$.
````
:::
::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
The area of a circle is $\pi r^2$.
:::
:::

::: {.grid .md-demo}
::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
````markdown
The pythagoras theorem:

$$
a^2 + b^2 = c^2
$$
````
:::
::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
The pythagoras theorem:

$$
a^2 + b^2 = c^2
$$
:::
:::
